function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here are some great ways to order a cake, whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty dessert, or a quick online delivery: | Option | What it offers | How to order | Tips | |--------|----------------|--------------|------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often handmade cakes in a variety of flavors and styles. | • Call or visit the bakery’s website.
• Many have online ordering forms or can take orders over the phone. | • Ask about custom designs, dietary restrictions (gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑free), and delivery times.
• Some bakeries offer pickup or curb‑side service. | | **Grocery stores & supermarkets** | Ready‑made cakes, pre‑decorated or plain, plus cake mixes. | • Check the bakery section in-store or on the store’s website.
• Many large chains (Walmart, Kroger, Safeway) have online ordering with pickup or delivery. | • Great for last‑minute orders or if you want a quick, budget‑friendly option. | | **Online cake delivery services** | Specialty cakes from artisan bakers across the country, often shipped directly to your door. | • Visit sites like **Goldbelly**, **BakeShop**, **Cake Delivery**, or **Etsy** (many sellers offer custom cakes).
• Select flavor, size, and delivery date; pay online. | • Ideal for special occasions (weddings, birthdays) or if you want a unique design.
• Check shipping times and any local delivery restrictions. | | **Meal‑delivery & subscription boxes** | Pre‑made cakes or cake kits delivered monthly. | • Sign up for services like **HelloFresh**, **Blue Apron**, or **Baker’s Dozen** that include cake recipes or ready‑to‑bake kits. | • Good for experimenting with baking at home or getting a surprise dessert each month. | | **Specialty dessert shops** | Cakes with unique themes (e.g., chocolate lava, fruit tarts, vegan options). | • Search for “specialty cake shop” + your city on Google or Yelp.
• Many have online menus and can take orders via email or phone. | • Perfect for themed parties or dietary restrictions. | | **Fast‑food & coffee chains** | Quick, pre‑decorated cakes (often small). | • Order at the counter or via the chain’s app (e.g., Starbucks, Dunkin’, Panera). | • Great for a quick pick‑up or a simple celebration. | ### Quick Steps to Order 1. **Decide on the occasion** (birthday, wedding, corporate event, etc.) and the cake size you need. 2. **Choose a style** (plain, frosted, custom design, dietary restrictions). 3. **Pick a vendor** from the table above that fits your budget and location. 4. **Place the order**—most places let you do this online, but you can also call or visit in person. 5. **Confirm delivery or pickup details** and any special instructions (e.g., “no sugar” or “decorate with roses”). #### If you let me know your city or zip code, I can suggest specific bakeries or delivery services in your area!
